PAINTING & BODYWORK · Painting

Full Vehicle Repainting in Riyadh

Complete vehicle repainting at QSC's Riyadh painting facility — for sun-damaged, color-changed or comprehensively restored luxury cars, with honest scoping first.

  1. Home
  2. Painting & Bodywork
  3. Full Vehicle Repainting

A full repaint is the most demanding job a paint shop takes on: every panel, every edge, every jamb decision affects whether the result looks factory or 'resprayed'. It is the right choice when sun damage is widespread, when a color change is wanted, or when restoration justifies it — and the wrong choice when a targeted repair would serve better. QSC scopes a full repaint honestly: what gets disassembled, how jambs and edges are handled, and what the realistic outcome is for the car's condition and budget.

A full repaint succeeds or fails on its boundaries: door jambs, engine bay edges, boot gutters, the undersides of sills — every place where new paint meets old tells the story of how thoroughly the job was scoped. A 'glass-out, trim-off' repaint and a 'panels-only' respray can look identical in photographs and utterly different in person three years later. QSC's scoping conversation puts these choices on the table explicitly, with the cost and the visual consequence of each, so the owner chooses the standard knowingly rather than discovering it later.

The repaint process at the Fast Painting facility runs in documented stages: full assessment with paint-depth readings across every panel; strip or sand decisions per panel based on what the readings reveal; substrate repair and corrosion treatment wherever found; then the build of primer, color and clear in controlled conditions with flash times respected. Photographs at each stage become part of the car's file — evidence of what is under the new finish, which serious buyers of repainted luxury cars increasingly ask to see.

When to book this service

  • Widespread fading, clearcoat failure or oxidation across multiple panels
  • A desired color change for the whole vehicle
  • A restoration project that includes complete refinishing
  • Accumulated mismatched repairs you want unified

Cost and time — honestly

Pricing at QSC follows the assessment, never precedes it: after evaluation you receive the proposed scope and its cost for approval, and only what you approve is carried out. Durations are estimated realistically per job — we publish no blanket promises we could not keep for every case.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Does a full repaint lower my car's value?

A documented, high-quality repaint on a car whose paint had genuinely failed usually helps, not hurts. What damages value is undisclosed or poor-quality paintwork — which is exactly what proper scoping and documentation avoid.

Can I change the color completely?

Yes — a color change is scoped with jambs, engine bay and boot surfaces discussed explicitly, since how far the new color extends is the main cost and quality decision. Regulatory notification requirements for color changes are yours to complete; the workshop will remind you.

Full repaint or panel repairs — how do I choose?

Send photos of the car for an initial view, then bring it in. The honest answer depends on how many panels are affected and the condition beneath; sometimes the cheaper targeted path is genuinely the better one, and the assessment will say so.

Will you repaint over my existing paint or strip it?

Per panel, the readings decide: sound factory paint within thickness limits is an excellent base; panels with thick old refinish layers, damage history or adhesion doubt get taken further down. Blanket answers either way would be dishonest — the measurement tells us what each panel needs.
